clue.text: Sort of ship providing contents for earth

indicators.note: the following pieces are said to be the filling of the earth word, so they go inside it

parts.note: clay is a kind of earth or soil
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
providing means if, as in 'providing it rains'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what kind of vessel would carry a cargo of soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of ship' reads as one phrase, but 'Sort' is the definition, a verb; 'contents for' signals the filling of the earth word.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to arrange them into groups or categories, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Queens, perhaps, go out with funny people

parts.note: to court someone is to go out with them romantically
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: Some queens date a group of comedians.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens look like monarchs, but the 'perhaps' points to the playing-card sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings, queens and jacks are the picture cards in a pack, so queens are an example.

clue.text: £1,000 is in time to make richer

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds arriving on time would make someone richer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance or increase someone's wealth or power is the verb's sense of enrich.

clue.text: Description of 7 brutally forthright? Alas, yes!

definitions.text: Description of 7 brutally forthright? Alas, yes!

parts.words: Description of 7 brutally forthright? Alas, yes!
parts.note: 7 points to Ernie of the comedy duo with Eric Morecambe, who regularly mocked Ernie's lower limbs in blunt terms

explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy double act; Eric's running gag insulted Ernie's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Morecambe's catchphrase was a brutally candid description of his partner's legs.

clue.text: See 3
Cover for brave slaphead's accessory, cosy but not right

parts.note: a slaphead is British slang for a bald man, whose accessory might be a wig

indicators.note: the R, for right, is removed from the word meaning cosy

parts.note: cosy can mean warm and snug

explanation.surface: A bald man's hairpiece is described as snug but slightly off.
explanation.walkthrough: A brave is a Native American warrior, so his cover is a tent; 'but not right' takes R out of WARM to leave WAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee-style dome hut is the traditional dwelling, the shelter, of a Native American warrior.

clue.text: Equivalent to Bliss and Stravinsky engaging Pole for topless mazurka, perhaps

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the composer's name holds the pole letter

parts.note: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian composer
N is the north pole

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a mazurka is an example of a dance

explanation.surface: Arthur Bliss and Stravinsky, two composers, work with a Polish dancer in a mazurka.
explanation.walkthrough: Bliss looks like the composer Arthur Bliss, but the definition is the saying 'ignorance is bliss'; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that not knowing is bliss, so the two are treated as equivalent.

clue.text: In the know, I seem to be knowing

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone in the know claims to seem knowledgeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the know' reads as an idiom, but 'In the' signals the run inside 'know, I seem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knowing, shrewd or sagacious, is the adjective's sense here.

clue.text: Numerically, this clue's position may be described as perfect

definitions.text: Numerically, this clue's position may be described as perfect

parts.words: Numerically, this clue's position may be described as perfect
parts.note: this clue sits at number 8, and eight is a perfect cube, so the clue's number is perfect in mathematical terms

explanation.definitionFit: Mint condition means perfect, as new, the word for an item without flaw.

clue.text: Development of line after good input terribly hard

indicators.note: the first part of the word 'input' says the next pieces go inside
terribly signals that the letters of the word put are jumbled

parts.note: the second half of the word 'input', taken as letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the line word comes after the good letter

parts.note: a row is a line of things
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A development of a production line, after good contributions, proves very difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'input' is split in two: its 'in' is the container signal and its 'put' is the fodder that 'terribly' rearranges into UPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Upward growth is a form of development or the process of growing up.

clue.text: Harmony is the point in marriage

indicators.note: the point letter goes inside the marriage word

parts.note: a marriage is a union
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A remark that harmony is the essence of a good marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is the' are link words; 'point' is a compass point, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in agreement on one note, or general accord, is harmony in a loose sense.

clue.text: See 24
Express puzzle passed round, many holes in it

indicators.note: the puzzle word goes around the express word, enclosing it

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle
an express is a fast train

explanation.surface: A fast-moving puzzle circulates, and it turns out to be full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a verb but is a noun, a fast train, placed inside TEASER.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen strainer for tea leaves is a perforated device, literally full of holes.

clue.text: Rescheduling, points out beset by stink

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the stink word surrounds the jumbled letters

parts.note: pong is British slang for a stink

indicators.note: out signals the letters of points are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rescheduled event lets points escape, surrounded by a bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points out' looks like 'indicates', but 'out' is the anagram signal and 'beset by' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferring something to a later time is rescheduling it.

clue.text: A child's heading into 21, old? Unlikely!

definitions.text: A child's heading into 21, old? Unlikely!

indicators.note: the child's first letter goes into the rearranged letters
unlikely signals the letters are muddled

parts.note: 21 down is a word for the years thirteen to nineteen

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter

explanation.surface: A child entering the teen years is hardly old.
explanation.walkthrough: The C from 'child's heading' goes into an anagram of A, TEENS (the answer to 21) and OLD, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster passing into the years after childhood is a teenager, neither child nor adult.

clue.text: Tree with less on top, polled

indicators.note: polled means having its head cut off, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: having less hair on top means being balder

explanation.surface: A tree that has been pruned has less growth at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Polled usually means pollarded; here it beheads BALDER, removing its first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common tree of damp ground, of the birch family.

clue.text: Vet again concerned with finding piano swallowed by bumble bee, possibly

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the piano letter is taken inside the insect word

parts.note: a bumble bee is an example of an insect
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A vet checks again on a piano swallowed by a bee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like an animal doctor but is a verb: to check.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet is to examine closely, so doing it again is to examine once more.

clue.text: Outlaw rejection of headless honey lover by writing part in bar

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go inside the bar word

parts.note: a rod is a bar

indicators.note: rejection here means turning back, so the pieces are read backwards
by means next to, so the writing part sits beside the bear
the first letter of the honey lover's name is removed

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear famous for loving honey
a nib is the writing part of a pen

explanation.surface: An outlaw rejects a beheaded honey-loving creature by putting writing into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' reverses the beheaded bear plus the nib together, giving BINHOO; 'in' then places it within the bar word.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Sherwood Forest bandit is the archetypal outlaw of English folklore.

clue.text: Tragic princess remains queen, one in spirit?

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, known as Di, died tragically in 1997
remains, as a verb, means stays still
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The remains of a tragic princess and a queen suggest a ghostly presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a noun for a body but is a verb; the definition puns on spirit as distilled liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of whisky or gin works in spirits, a pun on being in spirit like a ghost.

clue.text: Old time, look back for praise

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: back means the look word is read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone looks back on old times with praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look back' gives OL, LO reversed by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or celebrate someone highly is a straightforward verb synonym for praise.

clue.text: Admitting defeat finally, so guessing cryptic clues

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the rearranged letters take in the final letter
cryptic signals the letters of so guessing are scrambled
finally picks the last letter of defeat

explanation.surface: A solver confesses defeat at last after guessing at cryptic clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' looks like it describes the clues, but it is the anagram indicator; the T from 'defeat finally' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hints or pointers offered to help someone are proposals in the sense of clues.

clue.text: 12's end — in numbers these follow for young people

definitions.meaning: the numbers that follow twelve, thirteen to nineteen, all end in the same suffix
young people aged thirteen to nineteen

explanation.walkthrough: '12' here is the number, not clue 12.
explanation.definitionFit: The thirteen-to-nineteen years are named for the shared ending of those numbers.

clue.text: Basic thing categorically followed by no?

definitions.text: Basic thing categorically followed by no?

parts.words: Basic thing categorically followed by no?
parts.note: read the clue as an alphabetical index whose first half stops just before the letters N and O, while also naming a fundamental unit of matter

explanation.definitionFit: The smallest particle of an element is the basic unit of matter.

clue.text: Intend to be tight

definitions.meaning: to intend is to have in mind as a purpose

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to have a purpose and to be miserly, two distinct senses.

clue.text: Possible reason why you've been foolish with your investment here, or been stupid?

definitions.text: Possible reason why you've been foolish

indicators.note: stupid suggests the words are muddled up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rueful explanation of why an investment went badly wrong for a gullible person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' looks like part of the confession but is the anagram signal for YOUR INVESTMENT HERE OR BEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying, credited to P T Barnum, explains that suckers are always plentiful, the reason a fool was taken in.

clue.text: Trousers held by peg put on the box

indicators.note: the trousers word goes inside the peg word

parts.note: a tee is a golfer's peg
Levis are a brand of jeans, i.e. trousers

explanation.surface: Trousers are pinned by a peg before being placed on a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast something is to show it on television, colloquially the box.

clue.text: See 24
Perceptive faculty of English, however, maintains relief expired?

indicators.note: maintains here means holds, so the however word surrounds the sigh

parts.note: yet can mean however
a sigh of relief is a breath expired, i.e. breathed out

explanation.surface: An English observer maintains that relief has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expired' looks like 'ran out' but means breathed out: a sigh of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision, the power of seeing, is the faculty of perception through the eyes.
